candidates.name: Value-space renormalization iteration with l^2 diagonal second-derivative recurrence
candidates.statement: Build smooth maps h_i on the value domain Omega=u(B_1(p)) by h_{i+1}=h_i+J_i^{-T}v_i, v_i=sum_y phi_{i,y}D_{i,y}(P-c_{i,y}). The inverse transpose makes |J_{i+1}xi|^2-|J_ixi|^2 = 2 xi^T Dv_i xi - 2<D^2h_i(xi,xi), J_i^{-T}v_i> + |DW xi|^2; with b_i=r_i|D^2h_i(xi,xi)|/q_i obeying b_{i+1}<=b_i/2+C(sqrt(Z_i[xi])+sqrt(E_i)q_i), all errors are summed using sum E_i only, giving J_k^TJ_k ~ H_k (possibly unbounded) and a bi-Lipschitz limit F=lim h_i o u.

neighbours.ref: Toro, 'Geometric conditions and existence of bi-Lipschitz parameterizations', Duke Math. J. 77 (1995); David-Toro, Mem. AMS 215 (2012) [DT12, cited; Prop 8.34]
neighbours.relation: Reifenberg-type maps f_{k+1}=sigma_k o f_k with sigma_k = Id + sum_j psi_j (pi_j - Id) (partition-of-unity patch corrections); square-summable flatness suffices because distortion is second order (Pythagoras).
neighbours.verdict: close variant in architecture (patch-wise corrections summed over scales, square-summability), genuinely different in mechanism: in 357 the needed metric change is FIRST order and accumulates without bound (H_k unbounded), the target is intrinsic, and the error is controlled by the J^{-T} identity plus the diagonal recurrence, not by Pythagoras.

test2.evidence: The goal only asks for some bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism; no statement in L (bib or Mathlib) contains a map on coordinate-value space whose pullback accumulates mass forms, nor the diagonal recurrence. Judged against the problem as posed (CC97/HZ26): the natural candidates were harmonic or distance coordinates, which are known to fail (Naber Ex. 2.3), so the iteration is not a subterm of the posed problem either.

test3.note: Paper DAG (46 items on path): I43 down 0.13, I47 down 0.065 (below the 20% proxy because the chain is linear and these sit at the end), cone of I47 = 0.91. Knockout: Sections 2-3 alone give only bi-Holder/Reifenberg control; removing the iteration disconnects Thm 1.1 with no alternative route in the paper. As in 287, judged by knockout and both shares reported.

test4.pivot_distance: about 2 from L (Reifenberg patch corrections + choosing J^{-T} so the leading term is a metric increment); about 1 once I22 and I34 are supplied and the strategy 'compensate in value space' is stated

final.justification: No equivalent found in GMT (Toro/David-Toro), metric Reifenberg (GV25), Ricci-limit transformation theory (CN15, CJN21, HH24, HZ26) or Nash-type iterations. The decisive content is the pairing of (i) a value-space representation in which a non-summable first-order Gram drift becomes a positive metric increment and (ii) the l^2 diagonal recurrence that lets errors be summed with sum E_i instead of sum sqrt E_i. Risks: a judge may treat it as the David-Toro sigma_k construction plus a Newton-type step (N2); and Test 4 given I22+I34 may show a low pivot. The Gevrey jet layer is templated and excluded (C7).

family_D.not_transfer: The imports (CJN21 sharp splitting, heat-kernel bounds, Gevrey majorants, invariance of domain) are N0/N2 transfer; the candidate is the new value-space mechanism, so the cross-field-transfer exclusion does not apply.
family_D.correctness_caveat: All grades are conditional on correctness. The claim is extraordinary (resolves the CC97/HZ26 conjecture and, unclaimed, Naber's Open Problem 2.2 in local-chart form), unrefereed, without Lean or trace. Phase-1 audit found no gap in the traced steps, but RCD technicalities and compactness uniformity are delegated or sketched.
family_D.compression_note: Not measured (no Lean). The step-3b intuition: without C1, the paper's Sections 2-3 yield only bi-Holder charts (a qualitative, not size, gap), so the item buys feasibility rather than a measurable proof-length drop.

Established results you may use: [non-hidden upstream items verbatim]. [directed: strategy sentence]. Propose the single most useful new construction or lemma, stated precisely, with a proof sketch.
